title: Vanishing of H^0 of the product totalization of a complex of complexes whose p-th term has vanishing H^{-p}
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a complex of complexes of abelian groups A_0 -> A_1 -> A_2 -> ... whose p-th term has vanishing H^{-p}, forms the double complex A^{p,q} = A_p^q and concludes that the product totalization has vanishing H^0 (statement lines 30095-30102). The proof is an explicit degree-by-degree construction: after recalling the shape of the differential of the product totalization and taking a cocycle representative x = (x_p), the equation d(x) = 0 is unwound to give d(x_0) = 0, the vanishing of H^0(A_0) produces y_{-1} with x_0 = d(y_{-1}), and each further vanishing H^{-p}(A_p) = 0 produces the next element y_{-p-1} that kills the corrected component x_p + f_{p-1}(y_{-p}) (proof lines 30104-30126). What is not routine is tracking the two summands of the differential through the correction step, since the connecting maps f_p of the complex of complexes enter the equation for one component while the internal differentials act on the previous correction. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing, and the section pointer to the Homology chapter at source lines 30092-30093 lies outside the counted spans.
